observations.observation: Read-only config can serve inspection, but Claude attempts config lock and temporary writes and writes cache outside that root.
observations.implication: Materialization must expose a provider-specific writable runtime state even when the profile revision is immutable.

observations.observation: Copied OAuth and Bedrock, Vertex, or Foundry route selection can report configured or logged-in while an actual request is not usable.
observations.implication: Route selection, credential detection, validation, and last verification time are separate states.

observations.observation: Authenticated crash and resume was not proven because the available copied OAuth credential was expired.
observations.implication: Claude recovery remains a release blocker for its provider conformance suite, not a reason to weaken the generic lifecycle model.

observations.observation: System-managed allowManagedHooksOnly suppressed a user hook while a managed hook executed. policyHelper ran at startup and refresh; startup failure stopped launch, while background failure kept the process alive and retained the last policy.
observations.implication: Managed policy is a live authority binding, not profile content. AR must fail closed when no valid authority exists and must not interrupt a session for ordinary preference drift.

observations.observation: Project configuration follows the actual process working directory; the -C argument alone did not select the project layer.
observations.implication: The Codex materializer must treat process cwd as protocol-significant launch state.

observations.observation: Native inspection excludes an untrusted project config from the effective layer while project .agents skills remain discoverable.
observations.implication: Workspace trust and extension discovery require separate capability enforcement; config trust alone is insufficient.

observations.observation: Execution fails with a fully read-only CODEX_HOME because Codex needs installation identity, SQLite state, and temporary files.
observations.implication: Use a writable runtime CODEX_HOME with immutable config linked or copied into it and hash-verified.

observations.observation: The same app-server process immediately observed a changed config file.
observations.implication: A pinned session cannot reference mutable ambient Codex config paths.

observations.observation: The same app-server returned changed /etc/codex/requirements.toml constraints on a later configRequirements/read and returned a typed error after the file became invalid.
observations.implication: Codex requirements can be re-observed in process, but AR still needs its own authority revision and cannot infer that every active provider operation hot-applied the change.

observations.observation: After SIGKILL during a shell execution, five of five new processes resumed the same thread and recovered history.
observations.implication: History recovery is supported, but external effects remain outcome-unknown and require reconciliation rather than blind retry.

observations.observation: Two persisted executions succeeded with a shared writable CODEX_HOME and with isolated roots, using distinct threads.
observations.implication: This is a positive compatibility signal, not proof that refresh, cache, or all SQLite races are safe; AR should still isolate mutable session state.

observations.observation: Observed order is global, explicit config, project, then OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT for the installed binary.
observations.implication: The provider adapter must declare precedence as a BinaryRevision capability rather than a universal core rule.

observations.observation: Fifty cold starts selected duplicate skill IDs from project, global, and compatibility sources with varying winners.
observations.implication: Ambiguous skill IDs must require an explicit override or fail materialization for this binary capability set.

observations.observation: Read-only XDG_CONFIG_HOME with writable data, state, and cache supports inspection and a full ACP prompt.
observations.implication: OpenCode materialization can mount an immutable config revision while keeping provider state separate.

observations.observation: OpenCode 1.18.5 negotiated ACP v1, handled session new, list, resume, close, and an authenticated prompt; a v2 request cleanly negotiated v1.
observations.implication: ACP v1 is the first adapter; v2 remains side-by-side, negotiated, and feature-flagged.

observations.observation: An existing ACP process retained its initial config for a newly created session after the file changed.
observations.implication: Applying a new OpenCode profile revision requires a process boundary for this binary.

observations.observation: Linux /etc/opencode configuration overrode global and project values. An active ACP host retained its original managed revision, a new process loaded the changed revision, and invalid managed JSON blocked the new process.
observations.implication: OpenCode 1.18.5 requires a process boundary for managed-policy changes; revocation cannot rely on in-process config reload.

observations.observation: Session resume succeeded from 1.17.20 to 1.18.5 and back using the same session ID.
observations.implication: Pin BinaryRevision and allow migration only through an explicit compatibility matrix; this pair does not prove arbitrary upgrades.

observations.observation: Native inspection added a $schema field directly to writable ambient global and project config files.
observations.implication: Deterministic modes must run against a private immutable materialization, never the user's source config files.

observations.observation: Concurrent debug config and debug skill processes sharing one mutable OpenCode state root produced database is locked.
observations.implication: Separate mutable state roots per runtime instance and serialize operations that intentionally share provider state.

observations.observation: A synthetic project plugin executed JavaScript at startup and wrote outside the workspace but inside the sandbox.
observations.implication: Plugins are executable capabilities requiring explicit trust, grants, sandboxing, and audit; they are not passive profile data.

observations.observation: With --pure the project plugin remained visible in resolved config but its initializer did not execute.
observations.implication: Discovery and activation are separate states; conformance must verify execution evidence rather than trust config listing alone.

observations.observation: Claude --init-only executed a configured SessionStart shell hook outside the workspace but inside the sandbox without a model request.
observations.implication: Hooks require explicit executable capability grants before provider startup, independent of model tool permissions.

observations.observation: A missing MCP command and a delayed MCP server were reported separately; the delayed server honored a 500ms provider timeout and the command completed without orphan processes.
observations.implication: AR must still enforce outer startup and cancellation deadlines, but provider-level timeout and per-server diagnostics can be normalized.

observations.observation: A deliberately non-responsive synthetic MCP process was started by OpenCode, then removed with the provider process group when the AR-owned outer deadline expired.
observations.implication: AR process custody must own the provider process group and outer deadline; provider MCP timeout alone is not the cleanup authority.

observations.observation: A project .opencode skill remained discoverable after the synthetic workspace was copied to a new absolute path, with its location rebased to the new workspace.
observations.implication: Profile manifests store semantic source bases and relative paths, not fixed host absolute paths.

observations.observation: After deleting the active config file, the same ACP process created another session that retained the previously loaded command set.
observations.implication: Process continuity can mask missing files; AR must verify pinned materialization independently and cannot infer durability from a healthy provider process.

observations.observation: The active app-server returned a configuration-layer parse error on the next config read after config.toml was corrupted.
observations.implication: Provider behavior differs; AR must detect corruption, rematerialize the same revision, or block with PROFILE_REVISION_UNAVAILABLE without ambient fallback.
